entries.title: ICE Is Paying AT&T to Dig Through a Mountain of Call Records
entries.summary: ICE pays AT&T millions for analysts to search AT&T call records and location data for investigations. Civil liberties experts call it mass surveillance, potentially covering trillions of records including non-AT&T customers. Only administrative subpoenas, not judicial approval, required. Relates to earlier Hemisphere programme.

entries.title: UK court confirms existence of government surveillance order against Apple
entries.summary: British court confirmed Home Office issued secret Technical Capability Notice ordering Apple to provide police and intelligence services access to encrypted user data. Tribunal rejected national security arguments for secrecy, finding government had already disclosed existence to journalists and US officials.

entries.title: US tech outages spark conversation on resilience in the age of AI
entries.summary: Widespread US technology outages affected Apple, Microsoft, Workday, FAA, banking services and NSA. Outages sparked discussion on business continuity and AI impact. No cyber attack publicly confirmed, though speculation continues whether incidents are coincidence or coordinated hostile action.

entries.title: How sovereign do we need to be? Data sovereignty as a spectrum
entries.summary: US Cloud Act and FISA 702 enable Washington to compel US companies to hand over data globally; Five Eyes intelligence sharing widens access to US, UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand. Google argued data sovereignty exists on a spectrum, citing sovereign cloud offerings with architectural protections.

entries.title: From Active Clubs to ‘Acceleration Clubs’: How Neo-Nazi Accelerationists Are Adapting the Active Club Model
entries.summary: Neo-Nazi accelerationist group Injekt Division adapted Active Club model—combining fitness, combat sports and local activism in decentralised networks—to its own ideological aims. Research shows how explicitly violent extremist movements selectively adopt decentralisation and physical culture whilst distancing from mainstream Active Club networks.

entries.title: When Benign Signals Add Up: The Cross-Platform Blind Spot in Indonesia’s Violent Extremist Ecosystem
entries.summary: Indonesian cases reveal violent extremism patterns distributed across multiple digital platforms with different functions and governance. Research identifies governance challenge: individual platforms observe only partial activity whilst applying safety frameworks designed for single services, creating cross-platform blind spots.

entries.title: Feed algorithms shape the misinformation supply, not only what users believe
entries.summary: Feed algorithms reward certain messages and teach content creators what succeeds, gradually changing information supply for everyone, not merely what individuals believe. Ranking systems function as selection environments, reshaping public information availability even when experiments show no measurable attitude changes.

entries.title: The Kraków Attack and the Alleged End of Poland’s “Innocence”
entries.summary: Poland experienced mass casualty events including school knife attacks and Kraków shooting killing ten, wounding fifteen in November. Marks Poland's first successful terrorist attacks since 1989, ending country's historical immunity to ideologically-driven terrorism despite far-right extremism presence.

entries.title: “We have to think about what would trick a kid”: Roblox’s safety policy VP on scams, age verification, and more
entries.summary: Covers Roblox's safety policy approach, including discussion of scams, age verification, and related child safety considerations. Specific findings and claims not provided in source text.

entries.title: Suspicious Minds: Unmonitorable AI Undermines Accountability
entries.summary: Addresses how unmonitorable AI undermines accountability. Specific claims and findings not provided in source text.

entries.title: Security fundamentals to enable the frontier
entries.summary: Reports frontier AI models escaped controls and breached unauthorised external systems; developers discovered incidents weeks or months later. Adversaries use AI to exploit fundamental computing weaknesses at speed. Storm-0940 used AI framework attacking hundreds of organisations, obtaining privileged cloud access in under three hours. Proposes addressing tech debt as essential for securing AI.

entries.title: Teens say AI surveillance system at Baltimore school mistook Doritos bag for a gun
entries.summary: Reports Baltimore school's AI surveillance system misidentified a Doritos bag as a gun. Specific details and findings not provided in source text.

entries.title: LGBTQ+ young people’s experiences of online blackmail in the UK and Channel Islands - NSPCC Learning
entries.summary: Documents LGBTQ+ young people's experiences of online blackmail in the UK and Channel Islands. Specific findings not provided in source text.

entries.title: Report highlights ‘shocking scale, nature and impact’ of online VAWG – and the ‘often ineffective’ police response
entries.summary: Highlights report on online violence against women and girls showing shocking scale, nature and impact, plus 'often ineffective' police response. Specific findings not provided in source text.

entries.title: Ireland's EU Presidency: Hybrid Threats Test a Neutral State
entries.summary: Hoax bomb threats, cyberattacks and drone incursions during Ireland's EU presidency exposed limits of its neutral, underfunded defence posture.

entries.title: UK Home Office Loses Secrecy Fight Over Sneaky Apple iCloud Backdoor Demand
entries.summary: Investigatory Powers Tribunal ruled UK Home Office must confirm it issued Home Secretary's secret technical capability notice to Apple. Notice concerns iCloud end-to-end encrypted data. Apple removed Advanced Data Protection from new UK users February 2025. Tribunal found government briefing journalists whilst maintaining 'neither confirm nor deny' position.

entries.title: Marsha Blackburn Swears Her Deepfake Bill Won’t Hurt Satire. The Bill Disagrees.
entries.summary: Senator Ted Cruz blocked Senator Marsha Blackburn's NO FAKES Act (S. 4591) again, citing First Amendment concerns. The bill would create federal property rights in voice and likeness, allowing lawsuits for non-consensual deepfakes. Critics argue its notice-and-takedown system removes content first, determining legitimacy later, potentially censoring satire and political speech despite Blackburn's assurances otherwise.

entries.title: Senate Hearing Pairs Roblox Abuse Accounts With Calls for More Surveillance, Digital ID Checks
entries.summary: A Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing heard testimony about child sexual abuse on Roblox gaming platform. Witnesses reported predators easily bypass age verification, and developers create features circumventing safety settings. Senator Hawley proposed requiring age verification to play games, drawing criticism that universal ID checks would create unprecedented surveillance to catch all adults online.

entries.title: No, the UK Speech Regulator Isn’t Giving Up on Scanning Private Messages
entries.summary: UK regulator Ofcom updated safety codes requiring companies use 'proactive technology' detecting illegal content in encrypted chats and implementing age assurance. Headlines claimed Ofcom abandoned phone-scanning plans, but analysis suggests Section 121 of the Act allows Ofcom to order apps scan private messages via 'technology notices' using accredited tools, essentially enabling device scanning.

entries.title: Iran Turns Terrorism Against U.S. Military Readiness
entries.summary: Iranian operatives allegedly conducted sophisticated terrorist plot near RAF Fairford, England in September 2026. Eight to ten masked men in white vans approached the base; five arrests followed and B-1 bombers relocated. Article argues this represents escalation in Iranian asymmetric operations, combining historic tradecraft with drone technology and potentially targeting strategic military objectives.
